content.1_identity_verified:
- **Full name:** Frances Hellman
- **Title:** Professor of the Graduate School, Department of Physics, University of California, Berkeley (the Berkeley title for active emeriti; LBNL profile lists her as Professor Emeritus / Senior Faculty SE in the Materials Sciences Division).
- **Email on record:** fhellman@berkeley.edu
- **Affiliations:** UC Berkeley Physics Dept; UC Berkeley Materials Science & Engineering Dept (joint); Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Materials Sciences Division.
- **Research foci that match the brief:** (i) thermodynamics / calorimetry of thin-film and nanoscale materials, (ii) magnetic thin films / interfacial / skyrmion magnetism, (iii) amorphous / glassy materials (including low-temperature two-level-system physics relevant to cryogenic gravitational-wave detectors). The "gravitation" topic in the brief aligns with her Center-for-Coatings-Research work on thermal-noise coatings for LIGO-class gravitational-wave detectors.
- **Sources:**
  - https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/frances-hellman
  - https://physics.berkeley.edu/research-faculty/frances-hellman-group
  - https://physics.berkeley.edu/research-faculty/frances-hellman-group/people

content.2_recent_and_active_funding_announced_on:
Two NSF awards are currently active with Hellman as PI. Both were awarded through competitive NSF programs (DMR and PHY), not consortium/institutional/mission-budget line items.

| # | Award | Funder / Program | PI Role | Title | Amount (USD) | Award Date | Project Period | Status | Source |
|---|-------|------------------|---------|-------|--------------|------------|----------------|--------|--------|
| 1 | **NSF 2414027** | NSF / Division of Materials Research (DMR), Condensed Matter Physics | PI (sole) | "Investigating the connection between tunneling two-level systems, ultrastability, and ideality in vapor-deposited amorphous films through controlling disorder and fragility" | **$657,685** (Total Intended; same as Total Awarded to date) | 25 Jun 2024 | **01 Aug 2024 – 31 Jul 2027** (est.) | Active | https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2414027 |
| 2 | **NSF 2309290** | NSF / Division of Physics (PHY), Gravitational Physics / LIGO Research Support | PI (sole at Berkeley site) | "Collaborative Research: Center for Coatings Research" — Berkeley sub-award of a multi-site center | **$353,516 intended; $423,516 awarded to date** | 02 Aug 2023 | **01 Sep 2023 – 31 Aug 2026** (est.) | Active | https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2309290 |

Notes on classification:
- Both are competitive, peer-reviewed research grants (Standard Grant / Continuing Grant) awarded directly to UC Berkeley with Hellman as PI, not prizes or mission/lab budgets.
- Award 2 explicitly funds Berkeley's component of the multi-institution "Center for Coatings Research," which develops low-mechanical-loss amorphous coatings for next-generation (Cosmic Explorer) gravitational-wave detector mirrors — directly addressing the "gravitation" topic in the brief.
- No public source I checked links either award to a specific PhD hire; do not infer funded PhD positions from these awards.

Other potentially relevant items checked but not surfaced as new funding for Hellman in the window:
- NSF award 2011719 ("LSC Center for Coatings Research," 2020–2023) is **expired** and therefore out of scope; it is the predecessor of 2309290. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2011719
- DOE / Moore Foundation / Hellman Family Foundation awards to Hellman since 2024: **no verified public hits** in the search tools I could use (DOE OSTI does not expose a clean "PI-equals" interface, and Hellman Family Foundation grants are internal). Treated as "no verified public evidence found."
